decisive_items: Neck ultrasound failed to identify the thyroid gland in its normal pretracheal location
a 1.7 cm non-homogeneous, contrast-enhancing area at the tongue base with peripheral calcifications; several adjacent 1 cm nodular structures enhanced similarly to thyroid tissue
no thyroid gland was seen in the usual neck location
response.rationale: The tongue-base mass with enhanced thyroid-like nodular structures and absent orthotopic thyroid gland strongly indicates lingual/ectopic thyroid tissue rather than a thyroglossal duct cyst, which would not explain the absent normal thyroid and the presence of enhancing thyroid-equivalent tissue.

rejected.why: Although a thyroglossal duct cyst can occur at the tongue base, the absence of the normal thyroid gland and adjacent structures enhancing like thyroid tissue are more specific for ectopic thyroid tissue.
